body:
This looks like a more general way to implement https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13568 and similar. It will require follow-ups that adjusts behavior of other nodes (similar to what is already done in ScrollContainer), but it's a nice base I guess.

Seems like you need to do some cleanup (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/116640#discussion_r2840016204) before the implementation can be reviewed properly.

Looks fine overall. The modified controls (ScrollContainer, (RichText)Label) seem to behave as expected with maximum size, if you fulfill the requirements. I also tried some custom behavior using maximum size and it works too. The implementation seems to mostly mirror minimum size.

Definitely needs more reviews and discussion, as it's a rather major change, but it looks promising from what I tested.

> For Label, this is relevant when autowrap_mode != AUTOWRAP_OFF or when text_overrun_behavior != OVERRUN_NO_TRIMMING
> For RichTextLabel, this is relevant when fit_content = true and autowrap_mode != AUTOWRAP_OFF

This needs to be documented somewhere. Maybe description of each Control could have a paragraph about how it handles maximum size (only for controls that do handle it somehow).

Really look forward to this feature and took a bit of time to review today but will review more later: - `propagate_maximum_size` is a bit of a tricky boolean and I'm not sure we should introduce it with this PR. It propagates the max size to individual nodes which is a bit weird in the context of BoxContainers: … and it also propagates to grandchildren and beyond, even if those children are not in a container: I would argue that **the custom maximum size should primarily be set on the thing that has the potential to grow**, in the examples above: the Label and _not_ the PanelContainer. And with that approach we'd never need any propagation and thus removing one extra property and another layer of complexity – as well as remove something that may confuse new users (eg. "why aren't my labels growing?! ohh it's because 6 parents up something propagated all the way down here"). - I'd reorder first four properties inside the Layout section of Control to: custom min size, custom max size, (propagate max size here, if there's consensus on keeping it), and then clip contents. (and then layout direction, mode, etc) - Other than the above, I played around with Label and RichTextLabel and loved it! Precisely what I've been needing for the last two years. Will play with this a bit more later.

I haven't looked at the code, but the functionality and usability look good overall. The additional properties make the Layout section of Controls a bit of a mess, but another PR can attempt to reorganize and restructure all that.

There's some iffy behavior about the container sizing (`size_flags_horizontal` and `size_flags_vertical`) where expand (obviously) can't expand beyond the custom maximum size, and then the position of the Control inside the container is essentially 'undefined' – and I bet different depending on the Container attempting to position it. I guess that's somewhat expected behavior, but it makes the whole layout system a bit less 'clean'. 🤷🏼

Tested the latest version again and more in depth with different nodes. I somehow increasingly feel like we're opening a can of worms with this PR :P 1. The system has a conceptual limitation I don't think we can address, which is the vertical positioning of the PanelContainer2 in the HBoxContainer in the image below. If you want it vertically expanded to its maximum, it'll always be at the top and there is no setting that will change it – unless you don't expand but shrink to begin / center / end. I was able to work around it by adding a VBoxContainer in between where I have the option to do vertical alignment, like in the image below, but it's a bit messy. But, I'm prepared to accept this as a limitation to this already complex system. At least there are workarounds? 2. I found an issue with GridContainer where it appears the column width takes the smallest maximum width and sets all the items in that column to that? I would expect that only the item I'm adding the maximum size on would shrink while the other stay expanded. Here's a video of the current (unexpected) behavior: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5a3d9937-2471-4a7a-b84c-ebc963997b11 3. You can set the custom maximum size to a negative value. I don't think that should be possible? Can't imagine why that should be possible... 4. Didn't find any issues in ScrollContainer, FlowContainer, and FoldableContainer.

Your fixes for 1 and 2 work very nicely, actually. Much nicer than I expected. The fixes also add an alternative (perhaps less clean (IMO not a big deal)) method of 'filling', partially beyond the scope of this PR, that was previously not possible with BoxContainers: Messed around with the system once more with various Containers, couldn't find any issues. Great work @StarryWorm. Would love for the @godotengine/gui-nodes team to take a very close look at the code.

> Does it fill Godot's current limitations described in the proposals?

From my testing, it does.

> Are there any regressions? i.e. Bugs or performance issues if you don't set custom_maximum_size compared to the main branch

I didn't see any regressions.
As for performance... This makes size calculation more complex (although not much more than it already is). I didn't do any performance tests, however the editor is not noticeably slower at least.

> But I'm not sure if that behavior counts as A. expected nor B. desired. I would assume that implementing something like this could cause a lot of questionable new edge cases.

I think it would be more expected. The current size propagation is only useful for simple layout/single-child containers, like ScrollContainer or PanelContainer. But I suppose it would make the implementation much more complex, while the workaround is probably sufficient (i.e. set the expected custom maximum size for each child node 🤷‍♂️). Some introduced changes are already quite complex (like in GridContainer).
However the usefulness of the propagation property is questionable; this limitation should at least be better documented.

That said, the feature is fine as of now. It would be nice if you could also handle the maximum size of TabBar in relation to `clip_tabs`. It will be useful for #113051. I did some cursory test already and the maximum size fixes one of the problems in that PR.
The improved maximum size propagation seems ok, but there are problems with some containers.
TabContainer's popup button still goes out of bounds. Only happens if there is any maximum size assigned.

Tested, works correctly now.
The implementation seems ok, but the newest iteration is more invasive, with the addition of `get_bound_minimum_size()`. It's not a problem or anything, but it could use more GUI team reviews, to double-check it's alright.

Tested locally on all UI demo projects, it works as expected. There are however some visual changes that look like regressions: Demo | Before | After -|-|- Control Gallery[^1] | | Drag and Drop[^2] | | Pseudolocalization[^2] | | RegEx[^1] | | [^1]: Slight vertical shift in the text within the TextEdit node. [^2]: Larger buttons than intended. You can find the demos [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/gui). Font rendering might appear slightly different between screenshots, but I double-checked and it's not related to this PR.

Code looks good and seems to be working as expected.
